description: Operating System - Core software managing computer hardware, software resources, and fundamental system operations.
Basic Input/Output System - Legacy firmware initializing hardware components during startup and providing runtime services for the OS.
Unified Extensible Firmware Interface - Modern firmware interface replacing BIOS, offering Secure Boot, faster startup, and support for larger storage drives.
Trusted Platform Module - Dedicated cryptographic hardware chip on the motherboard storing encryption keys, passwords, and digital certificates.
Hardware Security Module - Physical computing appliance designed to securely manage, process, and safeguard enterprise cryptographic keys.
Central Processing Unit - Primary processor performing arithmetic, logical, and control operations to execute system instructions.
Graphics Processing Unit - Specialized circuit designed for rapid memory manipulation to accelerate parallel processing and graphics rendering.
Random Access Memory - Fast, volatile primary storage used by the operating system to hold active data and running program instructions.
Read-Only Memory - Non-volatile permanent storage used to retain critical startup instructions and firmware even when powered off.
Solid-State Drive - Fast, non-volatile storage device utilizing flash memory chips with no moving mechanical parts.
Hard Disk Drive - Legacy non-volatile storage device reading and writing data to spinning magnetic platters.
Redundant Array of Independent Disks - Technology combining multiple physical hard drives into a single logical unit for redundancy, performance, or both.
Universal Serial Bus - Standardized hardware interface for connecting peripheral devices and transferring power or data.
User Account Control - Windows security feature prompting users for permission or admin credentials before executing high-privilege system actions.
Access Control List - Table of permissions telling an operating system or firewall which access rights users or processes have to specific objects.
New Technology File System - Primary Windows file system featuring native journaling, access control lists (ACLs), and file-level encryption support.
Encrypting File System - Native Windows feature providing transparent file and folder level encryption directly within the NTFS file system.
Security-Enhanced Linux - Linux kernel security module enforcing Mandatory Access Control (MAC) policies to restrict system applications and services.
